## ROLEPLAY RULE 6. Don't use meta-information your character wouldn't be aware of.
Metagaming is a term used to describe actions based on knowledge during a round that would be inaccessible to your character. You cannot use information gained while you were playing a different character, while you’re a ghost, dead, in critical condition, or reveal information about who caused your death.
### Knowledge about antagonists (Metashield)
Awareness of what antagonists are capable of doing does generally not count as metagaming. The metashield prevents you from being able to use some information as an unfair advantage, including searching a PDA for uplinks without legitimate reason to suspect that the PDA was tampered with, or identifying chameleon gear without roleplay reasons (such as finding chameleon fibers.) Preparing for threats with no roleplay justification does sometimes count as metagaming, (such as hiding items linked to objectives and making them near impossible to retrieve.)
### Knowledge gained out-of-character (OOC)
No in-character (IC) information should be shared via LOOC/OOC, and no actions should be taken or altered because of LOOC or OOC chats, including deadchat.
### Knowledge from past lives
When playing as a different character (such as taking a ghost role), you are to act without knowledge of what occured in the round as any prior characters and as a ghost. Mindswap spells, and polymorphs are not considered changing characters for this rule. Brain implantation, cloning and borging applies knowledge lost upon death (NLR).
### Knowledge gained while in crit, knowledge lost upon death (New Life Rule, NLR)
Being unconscious (critically injured, asleep, or dead) prevents your character from remembering anything that happened to or around them while unconscious. If brought out of critical state to alive state, you may remember what caused you to enter critical state. Entering the dead state causes your character to forget the direct cause of their death. This includes who killed them, incriminating details such as any actions or events that immediately lead to their death.
### Knowledge that the round will end (and how your character will cease to exist)
Your character should or may be aware that their current shift will end and they they will return to Centcomm. They do not know that this represents the effective end of their existence from the perspective of their player. You cannot prepare for end-of-round griefing (EORG) or perform other actions that only make sense in the context that your character’s life ultimately doesn’t matter.
